connectors.description: Produces a linked (text, video) input pair on two ports from a configured source.

config_schema.description:
Configuration for a [`MultiModalSource`]: the `(format, kind)` selecting its
connector, plus a node-level `default_text` shared by every connector.

default_text.description:
A fallback instruction text used for any input that carries only a video and
no text of its own. When set, a connector may produce a video-only input and
this value is emitted on the text port for it; when unset, every input must
supply its own text (the prompt generator requires a text per video). This is
a node-level knob (not connector-specific): connectors read it from the shared
config via [`parse_default_text`](crate::connectors::multimodal::parse_default_text).

format.description:
The connector format selector (e.g. `"raw"`). Defaults to
[`MultiModalSource::DEFAULT_FORMAT`].

kind.description:
The connector kind selector (e.g. `"single_files"`). Supplied by the host that binds
the source to its inputs (the agent runner derives `file`/`s3` from their locations),
so it has no default.

config_schema.title: MultiModalSourceConfig

connectors.description: Collects one fitted Classifier per named head and saves a MultiheadClassifier bundle.

heads.description: Port names = head names, in declared order. At least 1, unique, non-empty.

path.description:
Where to write the fitted bundle (a safetensors snapshot loadable by
`atai_index::load_multihead_from_file`). A local path, or an
`s3://bucket/key` location (which requires the `s3` feature — otherwise
instantiation errors). Defaults to `fit-multihead-classifier.safetensors`
(relative to the working directory).

saved_parameters.description:
Arbitrary JSON saved verbatim into the bundle's `custom_parameters`
metadata (via `save_multihead_to_buffer_with_custom_parameters`). Unlike
`ClassifierFittingSink`, this sink never sees the input schema of any
head (that lives per-head inside each upstream `ClassifierFittingNode`),
so no auto-detected-column backfill applies here — the value is saved
exactly as configured. `None` (the default) embeds nothing.

upload_part_size.description:
Size, in bytes, of each part when uploading the fitted bundle to an
`s3://` destination as a multi-part upload (ignored for local paths). S3
requires every part except the last to be at least 5 MiB. Defaults to
50 MiB.

connectors.description: Writes incoming records to a configured destination.

config_schema.description:
Config common to every [`RecordsSink`]: a `format` and a `kind`, which
together select the concrete implementation. Both are required; any other
fields (consumed by the chosen connector, e.g. `path`) are allowed but not
constrained by this schema — the resolved connector validates those.
config_schema.title: RecordsSinkConfig

connectors.description: Produces a stream of records read from a configured data source.

ColumnSpec.description:
One entry of a [`RecordsSourceConfig::data_columns`]: a [`DType`] and, optionally,
the names of the columns of that type the source should produce. When `names`
is omitted/`null` the spec means "all columns that auto-detect as this `dtype`"
(for CSV, detected from the first rows). The connector reads only the selected
columns (plus whatever it needs to locate timestamps).

dtype.description:
The dtype of the listed (or auto-detected) columns (e.g. `f32`, `str`,
`embeddings(768)`).

names.description:
The names of the columns of this dtype to produce. Omitted/`null` means
"all auto-detected columns of this dtype". An empty list is a config error.

anyOf.description: Just the column name; the type defaults to `epoch_ms`.
The column name plus an explicit timestamp type.

type.description: How to interpret the timestamp value (defaults to `epoch_ms`).

TimestampColumnConfig.description:
The `timestamp_column` config: either a bare column name (its type defaults to
`epoch_ms`) or an object giving the name and an explicit `type`. To select a
`plain` timestamp you must name the column (there is no name-less object form).

TimestampType.description:
How a [`Records`] timestamp value is interpreted.

The stored value is always a `u64`; this only describes its *meaning*. Its config
string form is snake_case (`epoch_ms`, `plain`).

[`Records`]: crate::data::records::Records

oneOf.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch (the default).

A plain logical value — a step count or logical clock, not rooted in real
time / an epoch.

config_schema.description:
Config common to every [`RecordsSource`]: a `format`, a `kind`, the output
`data_columns`, and an optional `timestamp_column`. `format`/`kind` select the
connector; any other fields it needs (e.g. `paths`) are allowed but validated by
the connector, not here.

A session runs its own source instance, so it may name its own columns and decide how bad
cells are handled: `data_columns`, `timestamp_column` and `invalid_record_behavior` are
session fields. Which connector runs, and its own fields, are fixed.

data_columns.description:
The (non-timestamp) columns the source produces, grouped by dtype.
Omitted/`null` means "all columns, each with its auto-detected type". Each
[`ColumnSpec`] may also omit its `names` to select all auto-detected columns
of that dtype.

invalid_record_behavior.description:
How the source reacts to a record with an *unparseable* value (a bad cell):
the value is filled with a default and the record is handled per this behavior.
Defaults to `invalid` (mark the record invalid). Absent/empty values are treated
as *missing*, not invalid — they default-fill and the record stays valid. Every
records source is meant to honor this (some connectors may not yet).

timestamp_column.description:
Which column holds the timestamp, and how to interpret it. Omitted means the
first column, interpreted as epoch-milliseconds.

config_schema.title: RecordsSourceConfig

connectors.description: Consumes a stream of text, writing it to a configured destination.

config_schema.description: Dispatch config for [`TextSink`]: the `(format, kind)` selecting its connector.
config_schema.title: TextSinkConfig

connectors.description: Produces a stream of text read from a configured source.

config_schema.description: Dispatch config for [`TextSource`]: the `(format, kind)` selecting its connector.
config_schema.title: TextSourceConfig

nodes.description: Scores each record with a pre-fit LOF anomaly detector, emitting the predicted label per record.

ModelName.description:
The name identifying a model (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). A transparent newtype over
[`String`]; see the [module docs](self).

PcaSettings.description:
PCA settings for a [`DetectorFittingConfig`]. `std_floor` is deliberately absent:
it is filled from [`DetectorFittingConfig::zscore_std_floor`] — one floor, one
meaning, not a separate knob.

enabled.description:
Whether to reduce the embedding block with PCA before z-scoring/fitting.
Ignored (with a warning) when there is no embedding block. Defaults to
`false`.

n_components.description: Components to retain, clamped at fit time. Defaults to 20.

per_sensor.description: Fit independent PCA transforms for each sensor embedding column.

solver.description:
Force a solver, case-insensitive: `eigh`, `lobpcg`. `None` (the default)
auto-selects.

whiten.description:
Whiten the retained components (divide by their standard deviation,
floored at `zscore_std_floor`) rather than leaving a unit-norm projection.
Defaults to `true`.

config_schema.description:
Configuration for an [`AnomalyDetectorNode`].

`n_neighbors`, `metric`, `algorithm`, `pca` and `zscore_std_floor` are fit-time
hyperparameters that flow through [`TrainableNode::training_sink`] into the
[`DetectorFittingSink`]'s config when this node is the trainable head of an
auto-constructed training graph. They are persisted in the fitted snapshot and read back
by the scoring detector automatically, so a scoring node ignores them.

algorithm.description:
Fit-time: if set, force the index backend, case-insensitive: `exact`, `kd_tree`,
`ball_tree`. Unset (the default) lets the planner auto-select.

anomaly_label.description:
The label emitted for a row whose score exceeds the threshold. Defaults to
`"anomaly"`.

metric.description: Fit-time distance metric, case-insensitive: `cosine`, `l2`, `l1`. Defaults to `l1`.

model.description:
The detector to load, by name — resolved to a safetensors snapshot via the
runtime's [`ModelArtifactLoader`](crate::artifacts::ModelArtifactLoader).
There is no default: an unset model is a clear configuration error rather
than an attempt to load an empty name.

n_neighbors.description:
Fit-time: neighbours the density estimate averages over. Clamped to `n − 1` at fit.
Defaults to 20.

normal_label.description:
The label emitted for a row whose score does not exceed the threshold.
Defaults to `"normal"`.

output_embeddings.description:
Whether to copy each input embedding variate through to the output as a
new `embedding_{variate}` [`Embedding`](DType::Embedding) column (same
dim), matching [`ClassifierNode`](crate::nodes::classifier::ClassifierNode)
— for a fused input this includes the `DerivedFeature` pseudo-columns.
Defaults to `false`.

output_score.description:
Whether to add an [`anomaly_score`](ANOMALY_SCORE) `f32` column holding
each row's raw LOF score. Defaults to `true`.

pca.description: Fit-time PCA over the embedding block. Disabled by default.

threshold.description:
Overrides the artifact's decision boundary when set. Resolved once at
instantiation via [`Detector::set_threshold`], so scoring always goes
through [`Detector::is_anomaly`] and the boundary lives in exactly one
place. `None` keeps the threshold the detector was fit/saved with.

train_on.description:
Training only: the name of the blueprint's `metrics` target this node learns to
predict. May be left out when exactly one of the blueprint's targets is one the node
can learn. Must be written as a name, not a `${…}` reference.

zscore_std_floor.description:
Fit-time floor for every z-score in the pipeline, and for PCA's whitening divisor.
Defaults to 0.01.

config_schema.title: AnomalyDetectorConfig

nodes.description: Reshapes a MultiheadClassifierNode output row into the nested anomaly-event JSON contract, one serialized JSON string per row.

anomaly_head.description:
The head whose probability drives the top-level `anomaly`/`anomaly_score`
fields (kept separate from `events` since its positive label is
`anomaly_label`, not its own head name). Defaults to `"anomaly"`.

anomaly_label.description: The anomaly head's positive class label. Defaults to `"anomalous"`.

anomaly_threshold.description:
`anomaly` is `true` when the anomaly head's `p_{anomaly_head}_{anomaly_label}`
probability exceeds this threshold. Defaults to `0.6`.

events.description:
Head names to surface under `events`. For each `head` in this list, the
input's `p_{head}_{head}` column becomes `events.{head}` — i.e. each
head's own name is treated as its positive label (the convention every
n-shot head but `anomaly_head` uses: `{head}` vs. `not_{head}`).
Required — an empty list is a configuration error.

output_column.description:
Name of the single `Str` output column holding each row's serialized JSON.
Defaults to `"event_json"`.

nodes.description: Extracts a video's audio track as a decoded waveform.
Reduces each window to per-channel summary statistics (mean, std, range, min, max, slope, median).

features.description:
Which statistics to compute per channel, in output order. Names are
case-insensitive; see [`FeatureKind`]. Defaults to all seven in the
reference's order.

output_suffix.description:
Appended to each input channel's name to form the output column's name.
Defaults to `_features`.

**Cosmetic only.** `OmegaEncoderNode` names its embedding columns after the
same input variates, so without a suffix a fused schema would carry duplicate
variate names. The embedding/feature block split is derived from
[`FieldRole::DerivedFeature`], never from this string — so changing it can
never change how a detector interprets the vector.

nodes.description: Rejoins a conversation's turns and media branches into one multimodal prompt.
Fits a classifier from a labeled embedding stream and emits it once, at end-of-stream.

config_schema.description:
Configuration for a [`ClassifierFittingNode`] — the fit knobs only (no
`path`/upload: this node only composes into a `MultiheadClassifierSink`
downstream).

algorithm.description:
If set, force the index backend the planner uses, case-insensitive:
`exact`, `usearch`, `kd_tree`, or `ball_tree`. Unset (the default) lets the
planner auto-select.

k_neighbors.description:
Number of neighbours the fitted kNN classifier votes over
([`ClassifierConfig::k`]). Ignored for the `centroid` strategy. Defaults to 5.

metric.description:
Distance metric ([`ClassifierConfig::metric`]), case-insensitive: `cosine`,
`l2`, `dot`, or `l1`. Defaults to `cosine`.

normalize_embeddings.description:
If `true`, L2-normalize each example's concatenated embedding (per row)
before fitting. Defaults to `false`.

strategy.description:
The classification strategy ([`ClassifierConfig::strategy`]),
case-insensitive: `knn` or `centroid`. Defaults to `knn`.

weights.description:
Neighbour vote weighting ([`ClassifierConfig::weights`]), case-insensitive:
`uniform` or `distance`. Defaults to `distance`.

config_schema.title: ClassifierFittingNodeConfig

nodes.description: Classifies each record from its embeddings using a pre-fit classifier, emitting the predicted state per record.

ModelName.description:
The name identifying a model (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). A transparent newtype over
[`String`]; see the [module docs](self).

config_schema.description:
Configuration for a [`ClassifierNode`].

`strategy`, `k_neighbors`, `weights`, `metric`, `algorithm`, and
`normalize_embeddings` are fit-time hyperparameters that flow through
[`TrainableNode::training_sink`] into the [`ClassifierFittingSink`]'s config
when this node is the trainable head of an auto-constructed training graph.
They are persisted in the fitted safetensors snapshot and read back by the
predict-time classifier automatically.

algorithm.description:
Fit-time: if set, force the index backend the planner uses,
case-insensitive: `exact`, `usearch`, `kd_tree`, or `ball_tree`. Unset
(the default) lets the planner auto-select. `usearch` / `kd_tree` /
`ball_tree` require the matching build feature (`usearch` / `linfa`);
requesting one that is not compiled in is a config error.

k_neighbors.description:
Fit-time: number of neighbours the fitted kNN classifier votes over.
Must be at least 1. Ignored for the `centroid` strategy. Defaults to 5.

metric.description:
Fit-time distance metric, case-insensitive: `cosine`, `l2`, `dot`, or
`l1`. Defaults to `cosine`.

model.description:
The classifier to load, by name — resolved to a safetensors snapshot via
the runtime's [`ModelArtifactLoader`](crate::artifacts::ModelArtifactLoader). There
is no default: an unset model is a clear configuration error rather than an
attempt to load an empty name.

normalize_embeddings.description:
Fit-time: if `true`, L2-normalize each example's concatenated embedding
(per row) before fitting. The value is persisted in the fitted snapshot
and applied automatically at predict time, so a predicting
`ClassifierNode` does not need to set it. Defaults to `false`.

output_embeddings.description:
Whether to copy each input embedding variate through to the output as a new
`embedding_{variate}` [`Embedding`](DType::Embedding) column (same dim),
appended after the `p_{label}` columns. The values are carried verbatim,
including for invalid rows. Defaults to `false`.

output_probabilities.description:
Whether to add, per record, one `p_{label}` `f32` column per known class
holding that class's probability — its [`Prediction::votes`](atai_index::Prediction)
weight normalized so the per-record probabilities sum to 1; `0.0` for a
class that got no votes and for unclassified (invalid) records. Defaults to
`true`.

strategy.description:
Fit-time classification strategy, case-insensitive: `knn` — index every
n-shot window embedding and vote over the `k_neighbors` nearest (the OSM
default) — or `centroid` — average each class's embeddings into a single
mean prototype and label by the nearest class centroid (the Rare Event
Detection algorithm). With `centroid`, `k_neighbors` and `weights` are
ignored (there is one candidate per class). Defaults to `knn`.

train_on.description:
Training only: the name of the blueprint's `metrics` target this node learns to
predict. May be left out when exactly one of the blueprint's targets is one the node
can learn. Must be written as a name, not a `${…}` reference.

weights.description:
Fit-time neighbour vote weighting, case-insensitive: `uniform` or
`distance`. Defaults to `distance`.

config_schema.title: ClassifierConfig

nodes.description: Row-zips N Records input ports into one wider output stream, appending each port's columns in declared order.

ports.description:
Input port names, in the order their columns are appended. At least 2,
unique, non-empty, none named `out`.

nodes.description: Flattens windows back into a stream of their underlying records.

propagate_invalids.description:
Whether to carry window validity down to the records: when `true` (the
default), every record of an *invalid* window is marked invalid in the
output. When `false`, records are emitted with their own validity and the
window-level flag is dropped.

nodes.description: Decodes a request's referenced still images into RGB images, in request order.

max_images.description:
Most images one request may carry. A request naming more is refused; the cap bounds
both decode memory and the vision tokens the images expand into.

size.description:
If set, each image is resized to a `size x size` square, bounded to
[`MIN_MEDIA_SIDE`]`..=`[`MAX_MEDIA_SIDE`]. `None` keeps each image's own resolution —
images in one request need not share a size, since each is preprocessed independently.

Set or not, no image is *kept* with its longest side above [`MAX_MEDIA_SIDE`]: a larger
one is scaled down to it with its aspect ratio kept, so a 4000x1000 image becomes
2048x512, and a smaller one is left alone.

Together with `max_images` that ceiling bounds what a request holds: every image of a
request is emitted in one message, so its footprint is the sum of the images' RGB
buffers — at most 12 MB each, times `max_images`.

It does not bound the decode. A still image is decoded whole before it is resized, so
one image at a time costs whatever its source resolution costs. That is bounded
separately, by the decoder's own budget: a source too large to decode is refused from
its header, and the request carrying it is discarded like any other undecodable image.

nodes.description: Interpolates short runs of NaN values within each window's numeric columns independently (linear or forward-fill).

max_gap.description:
Only interpolate a maximal run of consecutive `NaN`s whose length is
`<= max_gap`; longer runs are left untouched (so a downstream validity check
still catches them). Defaults to `16`. `0` disables interpolation entirely —
the node short-circuits to a no-op passthrough (no buffering or per-window
rebuild).

method.description:
How to fill a gap: [`linear`](InterpolationMethod::Linear) (the default) or
[`ffill`](InterpolationMethod::Ffill).

nodes.description: Merges N named input streams into one output, in strict round-robin order.

BoundaryAffinity.description: How much of one port's stream an N-to-1 node keeps contiguous.

oneOf.description:
Race every live port every round. The default, and the only correct
setting for branches of one stream rejoining.

Keep each request bracket whole: hold to a port from its `NewRequest`
until the matching `EndOfRequest`. The setting for independent *served*
sources, whose requests are the unit of work.

Keep each input bracket whole: hold from `NewInput` to `EndOfInput`, so
every request within one input stays together. Note a served source opens
ONE input for its whole run and never closes it, so this starves peers on
that topology — it is for file/batch sources.

Drain one port entirely before reading another: hold from its first
message until its `EndOfStream`.

boundary.description:
The boundary this node keeps whole: while one port has a bracket of this
granularity open, the round-robin holds on that port instead of rotating.

buffer_capacity.description:
How many not-yet-emitted `Data` messages a single port may have
buffered ahead of its own round-robin turn. Must be at least 1.
Collection for a port pauses (applying ordinary backpressure to that
port's own upstream) once its buffer holds this many `Data` messages;
it resumes as soon as the round-robin emitter drains one. Signals are
never subject to this cap. Defaults to 1 — just enough for every
port's collection to make independent progress regardless of another
port's turn (see [`InterleaveNode`]'s doc comment); raise it only to
tolerate more sustained imbalance between branches before a port's
upstream starts feeling backpressure.

ports.description:
Input port names, in declared order. At least 2, unique, non-empty,
none named `out`.

nodes.description: Routes records by validity, sending invalid records to a separate invalid output.

keep_invalid_on_out.description:
Whether the `out` port mirrors the input verbatim (so invalid records also
appear on `out`, duplicated with `invalid`). When `false` (the default),
only valid records go to `out`. Either way, all invalid records go to
`invalid`.

nodes.description: Detects windows holding too many limit values (NaN or +/-Inf) or out-of-range values in a numeric column and flags or warns about them.

ValidationSettingObject.description:
The object form of a [`ValidationSetting`], and the single source of truth for its
field defaults and `deny_unknown_fields` behavior. [`ValidationSetting`]'s custom
codec delegates to this for the map case and reuses its schema (see below).

columns.description:
The `f32` columns (by name) to check. `null` (the default) means *auto*:
check every `f32` column. Named columns that don't exist or aren't `f32`
are ignored.

max_inf.description:
Reject a window holding more than `value` `+/-Inf` values (counted across all
checked `f32` columns). `value` defaults to `0` (any `+/-Inf` rejects).
Disabled by default.

max_inf_gap.description: Like `max_nan_gap`, for contiguous runs of `+/-Inf` values.

max_nan.description:
Reject a window holding more than `value` `NaN` values (counted across all
checked `f32` columns). `value` defaults to `0` (any `NaN` rejects). Disabled
by default.

max_nan_gap.description:
Reject a window when any single checked `f32` column holds a contiguous run
of more than `value` consecutive `NaN` values (per-variate: runs never cross
columns, and the count is not cross-column). Does not cap the total NaN count
(a column with a `NaN` every other record has a max run of 1). `value`
defaults to `0` (any `NaN` rejects). Disabled by default.

max_value.description:
Reject a window holding a checked `f32` value strictly above `value`. A
missing `value` imposes no upper bound (nothing is rejected). Disabled by
default.

min_value.description:
Reject a window holding a checked `f32` value strictly below `value` (so
`value: 0` allows only non-negative values, `0` accepted). A missing `value`
imposes no lower bound (nothing is rejected). Disabled by default.

nodes.description: Pairs an instruction with a preprocessed video into a manual-generation prompt.

system_message.default: You are creating an instructional how-to manual from a video. Watch the entire video and break down what is being demonstrated into a concise, ordered list of the distinct steps needed to reproduce the task. Identify each meaningful action as its own step, in the order it happens, and write a short, clear, imperative instruction describing what to do in that step (for example 'Fill the kettle with clean water'). Do not merge unrelated actions into one step, and do not pad the manual with trivial or repeated steps. Each video frame is preceded by a marker giving its real time in the video, written as '<T.T seconds>' (for example '<31.2 seconds>'). These markers are NOT uniformly spaced. For every step, set timestamp_start and timestamp_end to the real times of the frames where that step begins and ends, read from the nearest '<T.T seconds>' markers and written as clock time 'mm:ss' (for example 4 minutes and 5 seconds is written '04:05'). Do not invent evenly-spaced or round timestamps -- use the actual marker values, which span the whole video. Respond with exactly one line per step in the format 'Step N, timestamp_start: <mm:ss>, timestamp_end: <mm:ss>, instruction: <instruction>', where N is the step's number written as a plain integer starting at 0 (the first step is 'Step 0,', the second is 'Step 1,', and so on -- write the actual digit, never the letter 'N'). The timestamps must be the real marker times you observed for each step and should progress through the video as the steps occur, not cluster near the start. The steps happen in sequence and must not overlap in time: each step's timestamp_start must be greater than or equal to the previous step's timestamp_end, so Step 1 starts only after Step 0 ends, Step 2 starts only after Step 1 ends, and so on. Within a step, timestamp_end must be greater than timestamp_start. It is OK if there are temporal gaps between the steps. List the steps in the order they occur, one line each, and output nothing else.
system_message.description:
The system message placed first in every prompt's `input_messages`. Defaults
to the research manual-generation system prompt ([`DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGE`]).

default_config.system_message: You are creating an instructional how-to manual from a video. Watch the entire video and break down what is being demonstrated into a concise, ordered list of the distinct steps needed to reproduce the task. Identify each meaningful action as its own step, in the order it happens, and write a short, clear, imperative instruction describing what to do in that step (for example 'Fill the kettle with clean water'). Do not merge unrelated actions into one step, and do not pad the manual with trivial or repeated steps. Each video frame is preceded by a marker giving its real time in the video, written as '<T.T seconds>' (for example '<31.2 seconds>'). These markers are NOT uniformly spaced. For every step, set timestamp_start and timestamp_end to the real times of the frames where that step begins and ends, read from the nearest '<T.T seconds>' markers and written as clock time 'mm:ss' (for example 4 minutes and 5 seconds is written '04:05'). Do not invent evenly-spaced or round timestamps -- use the actual marker values, which span the whole video. Respond with exactly one line per step in the format 'Step N, timestamp_start: <mm:ss>, timestamp_end: <mm:ss>, instruction: <instruction>', where N is the step's number written as a plain integer starting at 0 (the first step is 'Step 0,', the second is 'Step 1,', and so on -- write the actual digit, never the letter 'N'). The timestamps must be the real marker times you observed for each step and should progress through the video as the steps occur, not cluster near the start. The steps happen in sequence and must not overlap in time: each step's timestamp_start must be greater than or equal to the previous step's timestamp_end, so Step 1 starts only after Step 0 ends, Step 2 starts only after Step 1 ends, and so on. Within a step, timestamp_end must be greater than timestamp_start. It is OK if there are temporal gaps between the steps. List the steps in the order they occur, one line each, and output nothing else.

config_schema.description: Configuration shared by every results-parser node.

compute_stats.description:
Whether to compute template-conformance stats (a streaming port of the research
`_compute_format_stats`) and attach them under `result_parser_stats` on the
emitted `EndOfRequest` metadata. Off by default.

output_frame_indices.description:
Whether to emit the `frame_start`/`frame_end` columns (the original-video frame
indices derived from the timestamps and the source fps). On by default.

config_schema.title: ResultsParserConfig

nodes.description: Merges N named input streams into one output, nondeterministically (whichever port is ready first).

BoundaryAffinity.description: How much of one port's stream an N-to-1 node keeps contiguous.

oneOf.description:
Race every live port every round. The default, and the only correct
setting for branches of one stream rejoining.

Keep each request bracket whole: hold to a port from its `NewRequest`

Keep each input bracket whole: hold from `NewInput` to `EndOfInput`, so
every request within one input stays together. Note a served source opens
ONE input for its whole run and never closes it, so this starves peers on

Drain one port entirely before reading another: hold from its first
message until its `EndOfStream`.

boundary.description:
The boundary this node keeps whole when merging: while one port has a
bracket of this granularity open, only that port is polled.

ports.description:
Input port names, in declared order. At least 2, unique, non-empty,
none named `out`.

nodes.description: Classifies each record against every head of a pre-fit MultiheadClassifier bundle, emitting the predicted state per head.

ModelName.description:
The name identifying a model (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). A transparent newtype over
[`String`]; see the [module docs](self).

model.description:
The multihead classifier bundle to load, by name — resolved to a
safetensors snapshot via the runtime's
[`ModelArtifactLoader`](crate::artifacts::ModelArtifactLoader). There is no
default: an unset model is a clear configuration error rather than an
attempt to load an empty name.

output_embeddings.description:
Whether to copy each input embedding variate through to the output as a
new `embedding_{variate}` [`Embedding`](DType::Embedding) column (same
dim). Defaults to `false`.

output_predicted_state.description:
Whether to add, per head, a `predicted_state_{head}` `Str` column holding
that head's predicted label (or `INVALID_STATE`/empty per the usual
invalid-record / abstention rules). Defaults to `true`. Set `false` to
drop these columns — e.g. when only the per-head probabilities
([`output_probabilities`](Self::output_probabilities)) are needed.

output_probabilities.description:
Whether to add, per head, one `p_{head}_{label}` `f32` column per known
class holding that class's probability. Defaults to `true`.

nodes.description: Streams text tokens from a Newton C (c2.5 / c2.6) checkpoint for a prepared multimodal prompt.

ModelName.description:
The name identifying a model (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). A transparent newtype over
[`String`]; see the [module docs](self).

gpu_memory_utilization.description: Fraction of device memory this node may use. Default `0.9`.

max_new_tokens.description:
Maximum number of generated tokens, at most [`MAX_NEW_TOKENS_LIMIT`]. Must stay below
`max_seq_len`, which it shares with the prompt.

max_seq_len.description: Context window for prompt + generation, at most [`MAX_SEQ_LEN_LIMIT`].

model.description: Named checkpoint directory (a c2.5 or c2.6 checkpoint).

vram_reclaim_interval_secs.description:
How often the background reclaim thread samples VRAM usage, in seconds.
`0` disables the thread; request-boundary reclaim still runs. Default `1.0`.

nodes.description: Streams text tokens for a prepared multimodal video prompt.

ModelName.description:
The name identifying a model (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). A transparent newtype over
[`String`]; see the [module docs](self).

ToolAdmissionUnit.description: What admission counts and leaves out as one item of tool results.

oneOf.description: Every result of one step, as the research agents do.
One call's result.

compression_delta_sensitivity.description:
How many robust standard deviations above a clip's own median frame-to-frame change counts as
a scene cut. Larger is more tolerant of change (fewer, longer segments). Default `3.0`.
Ignored unless `min_temporal_similarity_threshold` is set.

compression_max_kept_gap.description:
Coverage floor: inside one segment, never leave more than this many temporal steps between
kept frames, so a long segment is not represented by its two boundary frames alone. `0`
removes the floor. Default `4`, matching the reference. Ignored unless
`min_temporal_similarity_threshold` is set.

enable_thinking.description:
Hint passed to the chat template as its `enable_thinking` variable. Defaults to `true`, so
a template that honours it renders a reasoning prompt.

A *hint*, not a switch: whether a reasoning block is opened is decided by the template, and
a template is free to ignore this. The shipped f1.0 one does — it renders a bare
`<|im_start|>assistant\n` and lets the model open and close its own block, which reaches
the same place by a route that can actually terminate. Nothing downstream reads this flag
to decide how to parse the output; that is measured on the rendered prompt instead.

gpu_memory_utilization.description: Fraction of device memory this node may use. Default `0.9`.

keep_recent_results.description:
When a generation does not fit the context, how many of the most recent items of tool
results are never left out: a request that does not fit without them ends instead. `0`, the
default, keeps none. Ignored when `tools` is empty.

max_new_tokens.description:
Maximum number of generated tokens, at most [`MAX_NEW_TOKENS_LIMIT`]. Must leave room for
the prompt inside the model's context window: this has to stay *below* `max_seq_len`, so
requesting the cap here also requires raising the window above it.

max_seq_len.description: Context window for prompt + generation, at most [`MAX_SEQ_LEN_LIMIT`].

max_tool_steps.description:
How many of a request's generations may call tools. Once that many have, the model is
given one more generation, with no tools offered, and asked for its final answer. `0`
offers no tools at all. Ignored when `tools` is empty.

**Each step is a full generation**: the whole conversation is re-rendered and the clip is
re-encoded through the vision tower, because the engine has no prefix cache. A tool-using
request can therefore cost up to this many plus one times a plain one, which is why the
default is 3 rather than the OpenAI node's 8.

The request's closing boundary records how it ended under `termination`.

min_temporal_similarity_threshold.description:
Enables temporal frame compression: consecutive video frames at least this similar are
treated as one segment, and only its boundary frames reach the language model. Shortens
prefill and KV occupancy on clips that hold still.

Defaults to `0.0`, which is compression **on** with no similarity floor.

`null` disables compression and submits every sampled frame. Note that `null` and `0.0` are
opposite behaviours here, not neighbouring thresholds — `0.0` is the most aggressive setting,
not the least.

omission_notice.default: omitted from the prompt to keep room for the answer; this call and its full result remain in the run's tool transcript
omission_notice.description:
What the model is shown in place of a tool result left out to fit the context, alongside
the call's id. Ignored when `tools` is empty.

protected_recent_results.description:
When a generation does not fit the context, how many of the most recent items of tool
results keep their results the longest. Older items are left out first, oldest first, then
the prompt is replaced by its fallbacks in turn, and only then are these left out. Ignored
when `tools` is empty.

tool_admission_unit.description:
What one item of tool results is when a generation does not fit the context and results
are left out to fit it: a whole step's results (`step`, the default) or one call's
(`call`). Ignored when `tools` is empty.

tool_timeout_secs.description:
How long any one tool call may take before it is abandoned and the model is told so, in
seconds. `0` leaves tool calls unbounded. Ignored when `tools` is empty.

Applies to each call separately, so one stuck tool does not consume the budget of the
others it was requested alongside.

tools.description:
Names of the tools the model may call, looked up in the runtime's tool registry. An unknown
name fails when the graph is built.

Empty (the default) means every request is a single generation, streamed straight out, with
no tool-call parsing.

vram_reclaim_interval_secs.description:
How often the background reclaim thread samples VRAM usage, in seconds.
`0` disables the thread; request-boundary reclaim still runs. Default `1.0`.

default_config.omission_notice: omitted from the prompt to keep room for the answer; this call and its full result remain in the run's tool transcript

nodes.description: Encodes each window into an embedding using the Omega model.

ModelName.description:
The name identifying a model (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). A transparent newtype over
[`String`]; see the [module docs](self).

batch_size.description:
**Deprecated — use [`max_batch_size`](Self::max_batch_size).** Still accepted, and
used only when `max_batch_size` is unset.

batching_delay_ms.description: **Deprecated — removed, and ignored.** Accepted so an old config still resolves.

max_batch_size.description:
Accumulation budget for one forward, in the serving engine's own weight unit
(channel rows, for Omega). The engine decides how a batch becomes forwards; this
only says how much work it may gather.

Engine-wide: a graph joining a loaded engine gets that engine's budget.

max_concurrent_requests.description:
How many requests this node keeps outstanding, so the engine always has work
queued while an earlier result is awaited.

max_queue_size.description:
Backlog bound, in the same weight unit: how much admitted-but-not-yet-dispatched
work the engine will hold. A submit waits for its place in the queue rather than
failing, so raising this buys tolerance for bursts at the cost of queueing latency.

Must be at least [`max_batch_size`](Self::max_batch_size) — a backlog smaller than
one forward could never fill a batch, so instantiation refuses that pairing — and
should comfortably exceed the largest single message's weight (`windows x f32
channels` of the biggest [`Windows`](crate::data::windows::Windows) upstream emits):
a submit heavier than the whole backlog can never be admitted.

Engine-wide: a graph joining a loaded engine gets that engine's bound, so a message
heavier than it is refused even when this graph asked for more.

model.description:
The Omega model to load, by name (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). The weights are
resolved from this name via the runtime's
[`ModelArtifactLoader`](crate::artifacts::ModelArtifactLoader).

nodes.description: Fits LOF on each input file at end-of-input and labels that same dataset.

PcaSettings.description:
PCA settings for a [`DetectorFittingConfig`]. `std_floor` is deliberately absent:
it is filled from [`DetectorFittingConfig::zscore_std_floor`] — one floor, one
meaning, not a separate knob.

enabled.description:
Whether to reduce the embedding block with PCA before z-scoring/fitting.
Ignored (with a warning) when there is no embedding block. Defaults to
`false`.

n_components.description: Components to retain, clamped at fit time. Defaults to 20.

per_sensor.description: Fit independent PCA transforms for each sensor embedding column.

solver.description:
Force a solver, case-insensitive: `eigh`, `lobpcg`. `None` (the default)
auto-selects.

whiten.description:
Whiten the retained components (divide by their standard deviation,
floored at `zscore_std_floor`) rather than leaving a unit-norm projection.
Defaults to `true`.

config_schema.description:
Settings for fitting LOF on the current complete input file; no model artifact is required.

The detector fits afresh on every input, so a session may set everything that decides the
fit, the labels and the output columns.

algorithm.description: Optional index backend: exact, kd_tree or ball_tree.

max_neighbors_frac.description: Optional upper bound for K as a fraction of valid windows.

metric.description: Distance metric: l1, l2 or cosine.

n_neighbors.description: Number of neighbours, clamped to the number of valid rows minus one.

n_neighbors_frac.description: Optional K as a fraction of valid windows, capped by n_neighbors.

output_embeddings.description: Copy input embedding columns to the output.

pca.description: PCA over the leading embedding block.

threshold.description: Positive LOF decision boundary. Scores above it are outliers.

zscore_std_floor.description: Minimum z-score standard deviation and PCA whitening divisor.

config_schema.title: OutlierDetectorConfig

nodes.description: Accumulates SOP step strings into a single prepared-instruction string.
Routes each NewInput's records to the output port(s) whose configured condition matches its metadata.

Condition.description: A boolean condition evaluated against a JSON value via [`Condition::matches`].

oneOf.description: `subject.get(key)` equals `value` exactly. A missing key never matches.
Every nested condition must hold. `And([])` is vacuously true.
At least one nested condition must hold. `Or([])` is vacuously false.
The nested condition must not hold.

RouteEntry.description: One output port of a [`RouteNode`], with the [`Condition`] routed to it.

condition.description:
The condition, evaluated against a `NewInput`'s metadata, that routes
to this port.

port.description: The output port's name. Non-empty and not `in`.

routes.description:
One entry per output port: the condition that routes to it. The same
metadata can match more than one port's condition — e.g. two ports
both matching `state == "shared"` both receive it.

nodes.description: Validates each window for monotonic timestamps, a stable sampling rate, closeness to a target sampling rate, and the absence of large temporal gaps, and reports the average observed sampling rate.

ValidationSettingObject.description:
The object form of a [`ValidationSetting`], and the single source of truth for its
field defaults and `deny_unknown_fields` behavior. [`ValidationSetting`]'s custom
codec delegates to this for the map case and reuses its schema (see below).

ValidationToggleObject.description:
The object form of a [`ValidationToggle`], and the single source of truth for its
field defaults and `deny_unknown_fields` behavior. [`ValidationToggle`]'s custom
codec delegates to this for the map case and reuses its schema (see below).

max_sample_rate_variance.description:
Require the within-window sampling rate to be *close to* the configured
`sampling_rate`: reject a window when its observed rate deviates from
`sampling_rate` by more than `value` (a fraction). `value` defaults to `0`
(any deviation rejects). Disabled by default. Enabling this without
`sampling_rate` is a configuration error (caught at instantiation).

max_temporal_gap.description:
Reject a window holding a *temporal gap* — a jump between two sequential
timestamps — larger than `value` (a fraction) of the window's total span
(`last - first`). Catches data dropouts, independently of the overall rate.
`value` defaults to `0.05` (5% of the window span). Disabled by default.

report_average_sampling_rate.description:
Whether to emit the (informational) average-sample-rate events. Defaults to
`true`. Not a validation — a convenience report, unaffected by any behavior.

sample_rate_interval_max_outlier_fractio.description:
Allowed fraction of intervals between consecutive samples in a window that
may exceed `sample_rate_interval_tolerance`. Both shorter and longer intervals
count if their relative deviation from the median exceeds that tolerance.
Set `value` as a fraction: `0.1` allows up to 10% of intervals to exceed it.
The interval check fails only when the actual fraction is greater than `value`;
equality passes. An unset `value` means `0` (no exceeding intervals allowed).
Applies when `sample_rate_interval_tolerance` is enabled, and uses that
check's `behavior` to warn, mark the window invalid, or both.

sample_rate_interval_tolerance.description:
Require a *stable* within-window sampling rate: reject a window when the
relative deviation of its inter-sample intervals from their median —
`max(|diff - median|) / median` — exceeds `value` (a fraction). `value` defaults
to `0` (any deviation rejects). Disabled by default. This only checks the rate
is roughly constant within a window, not that it matches any target.

validate_monotonic_timestamps.description:
Require the timestamps *within a window* to be strictly increasing. A plain
on/off toggle (`true`/`false` in configs) — it has no threshold. Disabled by
default.

nodes.description: Copies every input, data and signals alike, unchanged to two output ports.
Pairs an instruction with a preprocessed video into a task-verification prompt.

system_message.default: You are verifying an instructional how-to video against its expected procedure. Watch the video and, for each numbered step listed below, decide whether that step was actually performed in the video. Mark a step PASSED only if it is clearly shown being carried out; mark it FAILED if it is incomplete, or performed incorrectly; mark it as MISSING if it is not shown at all. Each video frame is preceded by a marker giving its real time in the video, written as '<T.T seconds>' (for example '<31.2 seconds>'). These markers are NOT uniformly spaced. For every step, set timestamp_start and timestamp_end to the real times (in seconds, read from the nearest '<T.T seconds>' markers) of the frames where that step begins and ends. Do not invent evenly-spaced or round timestamps -- use the actual marker values, which span the whole video. Respond with exactly one line per step in the format 'step N: PASSED, timestamp_start: <timestamp_start>, timestamp_end: <timestamp_end>, reason: <reason>' or 'step N: FAILED, timestamp_start: <timestamp_start>, timestamp_end: <timestamp_end>, reason: <reason>' or 'step N: MISSING, reason: <reason>', where N is the step's number written as a plain integer starting at 0 (the first step is 'step 0:', the second is 'step 1:', and so on -- write the actual digit, never the letter 'N'). The timestamps must be the real marker times you observed for each step and should progress through the video as the steps occur, not cluster near the start. The steps happen in sequence and must not overlap in time: each step's timestamp_start must be greater than or equal to the previous step's timestamp_end, so step 1 starts only after step 0 ends, step 2 starts only after step 1 ends, and so on. Within a step, timestamp_end must be greater than timestamp_start. It is OK if there are temporal gaps between the steps. List the steps in the same order they are given, one line each, and output nothing else.
system_message.description:
The system message placed first in every prompt's `input_messages`. Defaults
to the research task-verification system prompt ([`DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGE`]).

default_config.system_message: You are verifying an instructional how-to video against its expected procedure. Watch the video and, for each numbered step listed below, decide whether that step was actually performed in the video. Mark a step PASSED only if it is clearly shown being carried out; mark it FAILED if it is incomplete, or performed incorrectly; mark it as MISSING if it is not shown at all. Each video frame is preceded by a marker giving its real time in the video, written as '<T.T seconds>' (for example '<31.2 seconds>'). These markers are NOT uniformly spaced. For every step, set timestamp_start and timestamp_end to the real times (in seconds, read from the nearest '<T.T seconds>' markers) of the frames where that step begins and ends. Do not invent evenly-spaced or round timestamps -- use the actual marker values, which span the whole video. Respond with exactly one line per step in the format 'step N: PASSED, timestamp_start: <timestamp_start>, timestamp_end: <timestamp_end>, reason: <reason>' or 'step N: FAILED, timestamp_start: <timestamp_start>, timestamp_end: <timestamp_end>, reason: <reason>' or 'step N: MISSING, reason: <reason>', where N is the step's number written as a plain integer starting at 0 (the first step is 'step 0:', the second is 'step 1:', and so on -- write the actual digit, never the letter 'N'). The timestamps must be the real marker times you observed for each step and should progress through the video as the steps occur, not cluster near the start. The steps happen in sequence and must not overlap in time: each step's timestamp_start must be greater than or equal to the previous step's timestamp_end, so step 1 starts only after step 0 ends, step 2 starts only after step 1 ends, and so on. Within a step, timestamp_end must be greater than timestamp_start. It is OK if there are temporal gaps between the steps. List the steps in the same order they are given, one line each, and output nothing else.

nodes.description: Parses the model's per-step task-verification output into records.

config_schema.description: Configuration shared by every results-parser node.

compute_stats.description:
Whether to compute template-conformance stats (a streaming port of the research
`_compute_format_stats`) and attach them under `result_parser_stats` on the
emitted `EndOfRequest` metadata. Off by default.

output_frame_indices.description:
Whether to emit the `frame_start`/`frame_end` columns (the original-video frame
indices derived from the timestamps and the source fps). On by default.

config_schema.title: ResultsParserConfig

nodes.description: Copies every input, data and signals alike, to N named output ports.

ports.description:
Output port names, in declared order. Must have at least 2 entries,
all unique, non-empty, and none named `in`.

nodes.description: Interpolates short runs of NaN values across the record stream (linear or forward-fill), before windowing.

max_gap.description:
Only interpolate a maximal run of consecutive `NaN`s whose length is
`<= max_gap`; longer runs are left untouched (so a downstream validity check
still catches them). Defaults to `16`. `0` disables interpolation entirely —
the node short-circuits to a no-op passthrough (no buffering or per-window
rebuild).

method.description:
How to fill a gap: [`linear`](InterpolationMethod::Linear) (the default) or
[`ffill`](InterpolationMethod::Ffill).

nodes.description: Patchifies decoded video frames into normalized video patches (Qwen3-VL).

VideoTimestampRule.description:
[`VideoPreprocessorConfig::timestamp_rule`]: how a temporal group's timestamp is derived from
its frames' source times. Rounded to one decimal either way.

oneOf.description: The group's first frame.
The mean of the group's first and last frame.

config_schema.description:
Configuration for a [`VideoPreprocessorNode`].

The preprocessing knobs default to the [`atai_video_preprocessor`] crate's
[`Config::default`](atai_video_preprocessor::Config::default), which matches F1's
shipped `processor_config.json`; a blueprint overrides them only to target a model
with different preprocessing.

batch_size.description:
Target number of frames per preprocessor push. The node buffers incoming
frames and pushes in full batches of this size (the final flush at end-of-input
may be smaller). Defaults to 64.

batching_delay_ms.description:
Maximum time, in milliseconds, to wait for more frames before pushing a partial
batch. Bounds latency under a slow upstream. Defaults to 200. `0` disables it
(partial batches only at an input boundary).

image_std.description: Per-channel std divided after mean subtraction (Qwen3-VL: `[0.5, 0.5, 0.5]`).

max_pixels.description: Upper bound on the spatiotemporal token volume (F1: 25_165_824).

min_pixels.description: Lower bound on the spatiotemporal token volume (F1: 4096).

rescale_factor.description: Rescale factor applied to raw u8 pixels before normalize (Qwen3-VL: 1/255).

temporal_patch_size.description: Frames grouped along the temporal axis per token row (Qwen3-VL: 2).

timestamp_rule.description:
Which frame time each temporal group's timestamp is read from (F1: `group_first`; C2.5 /
C2.6: `group_mean`).

config_schema.title: VideoPreprocessorConfig

nodes.description: Decodes a referenced video into sampled RGB frames using OpenCV.

FrameIndexRule.description:
How [`VideoReaderConfig::max_frames`] evenly spaced positions over a clip become frame
indices.

oneOf.description:
`np.linspace(0, total - 1, n, dtype=int)`: each position truncated toward zero, the
count left as sampled.

Each position rounded half to even, then the indices padded to a multiple of
`temporal_patch_size` by repeating the last one: the rule the C2.5/C2.6 serving decode
applies before its processor, which refuses a clip whose frame count is not a multiple
of the temporal patch.

ResizeFilterConfig.description: Which bilinear resize the decoder uses for [`VideoReaderConfig::size`].

config_schema.description: Configuration for a [`VideoReaderNode`], mirroring the research knobs.

batch_size.description:
Number of frames per emitted [`VideoFrames`](crate::data::video::VideoFrames)
batch. The sampled frames of one
input are streamed as `ceil(frame_count / batch_size)` data messages (all
within the same `NewInput`/`EndOfInput` bracket) rather than one object for the
whole video. Must be `>= 1` (enforced by the config schema). Defaults to 64.

index_rule.description:
How the sampled positions become frame indices. Defaults to
[`FrameIndexRule::Truncate`].

max_frames.description:
Number of frames to uniformly sample across the video, at most
[`MAX_FRAMES_LIMIT`]. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_MAX_FRAMES`].

A video with fewer frames than this is used whole; the cap is an upper bound on what is
sampled, not a requirement. Values outside `1..=MAX_FRAMES_LIMIT` — including the `<= 0`
"keep every frame" the research code accepts — are rejected by the schema when the
blueprint is resolved, so an unschedulable request fails before any GPU work.

resize_filter.description:
Which bilinear resize the decoder applies to whatever resize it performs — the `size`
square, or the scale down to [`MAX_MEDIA_SIDE`] an oversized clip gets with `size` unset.
A clip that needs neither is decoded without a resize and this knob does not reach it.

size.description:
If set, each frame is resized to a `size x size` square with `INTER_LINEAR`
(bilinear) interpolation, bounded to [`MIN_MEDIA_SIDE`]`..=`[`MAX_MEDIA_SIDE`]. `None`
keeps the source resolution and is the default, matching the research default.

Set or not, no frame is decoded with its longest side above [`MAX_MEDIA_SIDE`]: a
larger clip is scaled down to it with its aspect ratio kept, so a 3840x2160 clip
decodes at 2048x1152, and a smaller one is left alone.

config_schema.title: VideoReaderConfig

nodes.description: Transcribes a decoded audio waveform with Whisper.

ModelName.description:
The name identifying a model (e.g. `"omega:1.5"`). A transparent newtype over
[`String`]; see the [module docs](self).

cross_pool_budget_mib.description:
Cross-attention K/V cache budget in MiB. It bounds concurrently-decoded
30-second chunks; raise it for long clips or larger models.

cuda_ordinal.description:
CUDA device ordinal, matching
[`NewtonFusionConfig`](super::newton_fusion::NewtonFusionConfig): a graph running both
models normally puts them on the same card. Ignored by hosts built without a CUDA
Whisper backend, which load onto whatever device Burn resolves.

language.description:
Spoken-language override such as `"en"`. `null` uses Whisper language
detection from the first audio chunk.

max_new_tokens.description:
Maximum generated tokens for one Whisper chunk. `0` selects Whisper's own
default (currently 444).

model.description:
Named Whisper checkpoint artifact. Its resolved local path is a directory
containing `config.json`, `tokenizer.json`, and `model.safetensors`.

precision.description:
Model compute precision: `f32`, `f16`, or the engine's accepted aliases.
`f32` is portable; CUDA deployments normally use `f16`.

nodes.description: Groups the incoming records into fixed-size, optionally overlapping windows.

config_schema.description:
Configuration knobs for a [`WindowingNode`].

`window_size` and `step_size` shape one stream's windows, so a session may set them; the
compaction threshold is a memory/copy trade-off fixed per instance. None of them shapes the
node's contract (records in, windows out).

compaction_threshold.description:
Fraction of a source input that may be retained-but-unreachable before
the windows cut from it are compacted (copied) instead of kept as
zero-copy slices. `0.0` always compacts; `1.0` never does.

step_size.description: Number of records to advance between consecutive windows.

window_size.description: Number of records in each window.

config_schema.title: WindowingConfig
